items.title: The rotated triangle of an admissible short exact sequence is isomorphic to the cone of its connecting morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file dga.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-rotate-triangle at source lines 978-995: for a differential graded algebra A and an admissible short exact sequence 0 -> K -> L -> M -> 0 of dg A-modules with associated triangle (K, L, M, alpha, beta, delta), the triangles (M[-1], K, L, delta[-1], alpha, beta) and (M[-1], K, C(delta[-1]), delta[-1], i, p) are isomorphic. The proof at source lines 997-1013 is a direct comparison of differentials, and it is the identification that makes the rotation axiom work: it chooses splittings so that L is written as K direct sum M and alpha and beta become the natural inclusion and projection, then computes the differential of B (the middle term) as the block matrix with d_K, delta and d_M as its entries, observes that the cone of the shifted connecting morphism has the same underlying module K direct sum M and exactly the same differential matrix, and concludes the isomorphism from the identity of the two differentials. The whole point is that the two constructions produce the same matrix, which the statement does not display. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
